text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is using clear naming conventions. For example, a variable called "totalPrice" is much better than "tp". Functions should also be small and do one job well, so they are simple to test and reuse. When code is clean, it is easier to find mistakes and fix them quickly. This makes the software easier to maintain over time. In short, writing clean code saves time and helps teams work together more effectively.
